test_cases.query: Question: "Why is it recommended to perform group operations separately for each trading account?
test_cases.ground_truth: It is recommended because performing group operations separately for each trading account improves performance, particularly for bulk deletions, reducing overhead compared to handling orders across multiple accounts together.
_synth_contexts:
The bulk deletion works faster than the deletion of the same number of orders in a loop one by one using [IMTServerAPI::OrderDelete](imtserverapi_orderdelete.htm). The faster operation is particularly noticeable when deleting orders of the same account.

To improve performance, it is recommended to create arrays and perform group operations separately for each trading account.

test_cases.query: MTE+TS: which two prohibited practices—custom sync primitives on server threads & DB API calls in hooks—should be avoided?
test_cases.ground_truth: The two prohibited practices are: (1) using custom synchronization primitives that affect the operation of server threads, and (2) making calls to the trading database API (e.g., IMTServerAPI methods) within hooks or client base events.
_synth_contexts:
| |
| --- |
| All the plugin components must be implemented thread-safe, except for calls of IMTServerAPI methods. |

Multithreaded interaction with the trade server

We strongly advise you against interfering with the server threads operation and interaction logic. In particular, we urge you not to implement your own synchronization primitives affecting the server threads operation (i.e. not to use them in the [hooks](serverapi_hooks.htm)).

* Do not try to directly control the interaction of server internal threads by explicitly stopping them or applying synchronization primitives.
* The hooks and client base events (for example, [IMTUserSink::OnUser*](imtusersink_onuseradd.htm), [IMTUserSink::HookUser*](imtusersink_hookuseradd.htm)) should not contain calls of the API methods associated with the trading databases (for example, [IMTServerAPI::PositionGet](imtserverapi_positionget.htm)).

test_cases.query: What codes signal failure and when?
test_cases.ground_truth: Failure is signaled by error codes: MT_RET_ERR_NOTMAIN is returned when attempting to delete a configuration from a plugin that does not run on the main server, and MT_RET_ERR_NOTFOUND is returned when the object is not found. Any other error code indicates a failure.
_synth_contexts:
An indication of successful completion is the [MT_RET_OK](retcodes_successful.htm) response code. Otherwise, an error code will be returned.

Note

A configuration can be deleted only from the applications that run on the main server. For all other plugins the response code [MT_RET_ERR_NOTMAIN](retcodes_api.htm) will be returned. If the object is not found, the response code [MT_RET_ERR_NOTFOUND](retcodes_common.htm) is returned.

test_cases.query: When does MT_RET_ERR_DUPLICATE trigger, and which op requires sink mem pers?
test_cases.ground_truth: MT_RET_ERR_DUPLICATE is returned when the same IMTConVPSSink interface tries to subscribe to an event a second time. The sink object must stay in memory (i.e., must not be removed) until the VPSUnsubscribe call (or until the plugin is deleted).
_synth_contexts:
Note

Subscribing to events is thread safe. The same [IMTConVPSSink](imtconvpssink.htm) interface cannot subscribe to an event twice. The [MT_RET_ERR_DUPLICATE](retcodes_common.htm) response code is returned in this case.

The object at which sink points, must remain in the memory (must not be removed) until the call of [IMTServerAPI::VPSUnsubscribe](imtserverapi_vpsunsubscribe.htm) or until the plugin is deleted.
